items.speaker: Kamuta
items.text: What are you doing?!

items.speaker: Kamuta
items.text: How could you side with our enemies? Against your own people, against the ones who would rebuild our home?!
Incredulous severity colors his tone.

items.speaker: Kamuta
items.text: You've brought shame on our people. You've disappointed me.

items.speaker: Kamuta
items.text: Stop all this now, and come with me. We will beg Ms. Grace to cleanse your soul!
Like the countless times before, he waits for her to grasp his outstretched hand.
*thwack*
An unexpected act of defiance.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Joining Manus Vindictae was a mistake, Kamuta.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Their masks blinded our people, they tricked us with their lies and empty promises, but look! So many precious lives lost for nothing.

items.speaker: Kamuta
items.text: It wasn't for nothing. They died for the resurrection of Nukutaeao!

items.speaker: Kamuta
items.text: Isn't it your dream, too? To rebuild our home in a land free of humans and their wickedness?!
Fatutu shakes her head.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: No. Not anymore, Kamuta.
She looks around at her people, their faces marked with pain and confusion.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: We may have lost our islands, but what we've done here lost us something far more precious.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: There's nothing in this so-called "new era" that Ms. Grace promised us that is worth becoming monsters and corrupting our Spirit Shells.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Our pride must be in ourselves and who we are.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: The shells around our necks, the words we speak to one another, the way we treat others with kindness, not hatred. That is what defines us.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: We are more than just how the outsiders can use us, more than our Sea Mother's Eye. We are the wisdom of our elders, and the traditions we keep sacred.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: And if our islands all sink beneath the waves, we will remember them in our craft and in our stories, we will remember the story of the brave Nukutai girl fighting off the Serres, we will remember them in the songs of Nukutaeao!

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: No matter whether it's an island or a ship we stand on, as long as we're together, Nukutaeao—our home—lies beneath our feet!

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Didn't you say you would always have faith in me, Kamuta?

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: You believed I could lead our people to a better future.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Now, I believe in myself, too.
She raises her head, the shells on her chest heaving with every breath.
They tremble in unison, resonating with the collective energy of the Nukutai.

items.speaker: Kamuta
items.text: Heh heh.

items.speaker: Kamuta
items.text: You'll be a better leader than I ever was, Fatutu.
The expected reprimand never comes. She stares in shock at her brother,
at his lips curled into a faint smile, at his trembling hand still extended out to her, and ...
at the black blood seeping from his eyes and ears.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: What's happening to you?!
*crash*
The towering figure before her falls to the ground.

items.speaker: Kamuta
items.text: I'm fine, Tutu. I'll be alright.

items.speaker: Kamuta
items.text: You're right, dear sister. The words you spoke have opened my eyes.
Pained words are forced through his blackened lips.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Brother!
As she cries out, heads turn toward her.
The mask remains tightly affixed to Kamuta's face, its black liquid nearly covering it entirely.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's the mask's punishment!

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: I-I don't understand!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Manus Vindictae use their masks to sift out their most loyal followers. Those who pass the trial can retain their personality and memories.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: However ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: If they should show any signs of faltering in their faith, the mask will punish them. Their consciousness will be devoured by the fathomless depths of arcanum.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Until they become nothing but a walking corpse, caught in eternal agony.
A slow clap breaks the silence.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Well, well, I am stunned by the breadth of your knowledge of our operations, Ms. Vertin.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: But I must remind you: gossip like that is terribly bad manners.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Is it any wonder why our guests look so terrified?

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Though it does pique my curiosity. I wonder, even with all you said, do they fear us more than they fear death?
Her commanding gaze hovers over the ship's passengers before finally landing on her former follower.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: What a pity, Mr. Kamuta.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: I had high hopes for you. It seems our friendship has come to an untimely end.
Her words are cold and emotionless, instilling a new fear in the crowd.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The people here know the truth about your masks. There's no sense trying to deceive them any longer!

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Oh, is that so?
Grace slowly advances, her steps poised.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, stay behind me!
Sonetto imposes herself between the two, poised to fight.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Oh, what do we have here?

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: How adorable, the ever-loyal deputy leaps into action! *chuckle*

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: But we're on a tight schedule, and I don't have time to play games.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: There's no power in your shiny little badge here.
She glances at the Foundation emblem on her chest.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Mr. Kamuta, Manus Vindictae will forever remember your contribution.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Farewell.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Fatutu, watch out!

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: *Slæstu  í  djúpan  dvala.

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Brother! No!
The arcane fluctuations gently dissipate around Grace.

items.speaker: Barcarola
items.text: Captain Grace!

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: What is it now, Ms. Barcarola?

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: I'm sure you've already guessed this, but you've been relieved of your duties here.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Gaining the support of the Nukutai was never your purpose, am I right?

items.speaker: Fatutu
items.text: Ms. Grace, give me back my friends!
Grace ignores Fatutu's shouts and slightly furrows her brow.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: Oh, Vertin. I could almost delight in your cleverness, if it wasn't so damnably frustrating.
She snaps her fingers.
*clink*
A worn, oddly shaped Spirit Shell rolls to Grace's feet. She picks it up, as if greeting a long-lost friend.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: A pity.

items.speaker: Ms. Grace
items.text: But there's no turning back now.
The room falls silent once more. There is no sound but the howling of the wind outside.
A burst of static echoes from the lobby's speakers.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Hello! Hello?!

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Can't anyone hear me?

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: This is Ulrich from Laplace's "Storm" Research Group.

items.speaker: Startled Guest
items.text: Oh, dear!
The radio broadcast jolts the already frazzled guests.

items.speaker: Tinnitus-Stricken Guest
items.text: Whoa!
The tinnitus-stricken guest looks up, the broadcast still hissing incomprehensibly.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Everyone!

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: We've found a material that ...

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Our "Storm" problem is ...
The room falls briefly silent.
Then, it breaks into thunderous cheers and applause.

items.speaker: Tinnitus-Stricken Guest
items.text: What?
